claims.feature: other: divided reader verdict on the prose
claims.claim: The same book club reports its scores fell at the two ends of the scale, half at nine or above and half below five, averaging seven with nobody content.
claims.source: Andrew Mather, 'Book Club Discussion: Tigana By Guy Gavriel Kay', The Quill to Live, 17 Mar 2016
claims.quote: half of the group had scores of nine or above

claims.claim: The dissenting half of that book club called the writing pretentious and said they preferred more austere prose.
claims.source: Andrew Mather reporting the club's 'con' group, The Quill to Live, 17 Mar 2016
claims.quote: found the writing pretentious and that they preferred more austere prose

claims.claim: The same dissenting group found the pacing jarring because the perspective jumps from point-of-view to point-of-view.
claims.source: Andrew Mather reporting the club's 'con' group, The Quill to Live, 17 Mar 2016
claims.quote: the perspective often jumps from point-of-view to point-of-view

claims.feature: other: reader label for the register
claims.claim: A forum member characterises Kay's manner of writing as controlled and orchestrated.
claims.quote: Kay writes in a very controlled, orchestrated way

claims.feature: other: divided reader verdict on the prose
claims.claim: A forum member warns that a reader wanting a fast paced tight narrative will not suit Kay, while naming evocative prose as his best trait.
claims.source: a member replying at post #4, SFFWorld forum, 6 Dec 2011
claims.quote: His best traits are his evocative prose, quality characterization and flair

claims.claim: A forum member who reread two Kay novels back to back reports subtle differences of tone and manner of writing between them.
claims.source: a member at post #2, SFFWorld forum, 6 Dec 2011
claims.quote: lovely, subtle differences in his tone and manner of writing

claims.claim: A reader in a Goodreads Fantasy Book Club topic finds Kay's writing unnatural, saying he reaches for obscure words instead of his honest voice.
claims.source: Josh, message 8, Goodreads Fantasy Book Club topic on Guy Gavriel Kay, 27 Feb 2009
claims.quote: he tries too hard to wow the reader with tons

claims.feature: other: divided reader verdict on the prose
claims.claim: Another member of the same topic states she has no issue with the style and calls his use of language precise and lyric.
claims.source: Janny, message 12, Goodreads Fantasy Book Club topic on Guy Gavriel Kay, 12 Mar 2009
claims.quote: his use of language is precise, and lyric, and highly creative

claims.claim: The same member distinguishes Ysabel as quicker and less atmospheric, recommending it to a reader who wants a leaner prose style.
claims.source: Janny, message 12, Goodreads Fantasy Book Club topic on Guy Gavriel Kay, 12 Mar 2009
claims.quote: a reader looking for a leaner prose style

claims.claim: A member of the same topic describes Kay's method as travelling to a locale to absorb local colour and then writing on the region's theme.
claims.source: a member of the Goodreads Fantasy Book Club topic on Guy Gavriel Kay, 2009
claims.quote: travels to a locale to soak up local color

claims.claim: A reader-blogger reviewing Kay's whole run says Tigana's prose is very different from the often lean prose of The Fionavar Tapestry.
claims.source: Michal, 'Flippant Reviews: Guy Gavriel Kay', One Last Sketch, 12 Dec 2011
claims.quote: very different from the often lean prose of The Fionavar Tapestry

claims.claim: The same blogger says that in The Last Light of the Sun Kay's ornate style is cut down to a rougher language of sentence fragments and strong images.
claims.source: Michal, 'Flippant Reviews: Guy Gavriel Kay', One Last Sketch, 12 Dec 2011
claims.quote: ornate style is cut down here to a much rougher use
claims.page: post body, The Last Light of the Sun

claims.claim: The same blogger objects that the reader is too often told how to feel and given overwrought reminiscence about the lost province.
claims.source: Michal, 'Flippant Reviews: Guy Gavriel Kay', One Last Sketch, 12 Dec 2011
claims.quote: We’re all too often told how to feel

claims.feature: other: divided reader verdict on the prose
claims.claim: The same blogger names as an annoyance Kay's habit of long tangents describing the vast import of a historical moment.
claims.source: Michal, 'Flippant Reviews: Guy Gavriel Kay', One Last Sketch, 12 Dec 2011
claims.quote: long tangents describing the vast import of some historical moment

claims.feature: other: divided reader verdict on the prose
claims.claim: A reviewer for a fan site calls the prose technically superb and in the same review says it often felt cold and clinical.
claims.source: Alister, 'Tigana by Guy Gavriel Kay', Fantasy-Faction, 2013
claims.quote: the prose often felt cold and clinical, even lacking in emotion

verdicts.trueWording: half of the group had scores of nine or above
verdicts.note: Quill to Live post body, opening paragraph: quote exact; page also carries the other half 'below 5', 'a solid seven' average and 'no one seemed happy with the score' - every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: A few of the “con” group ... found the writing pretentious
verdicts.note: Quote exact in the 'Team Anti-Tigana' paragraph, including 'preferred more austere prose'; but the page scopes it to a few of the con group, not the dissenting half, so the reader-count limb overstates the source.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: attribution to the whole dissenting half: page attributes it only to 'A few of the “con” group'

verdicts.trueWording: Some found the pacing jarring as the perspective often jumps
verdicts.note: Quote exact in the 'Team Anti-Tigana' paragraph; the causal limb ('as the perspective often jumps from point-of-view to point-of-view') is supported, only the scope of who held the view is overstated.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: unanimity: page says 'Some' found the pacing jarring, not the dissenting group as a whole

verdicts.trueWording: Kay writes in a very controlled, orchestrated way
verdicts.note: SFFWorld post #5 by Erfael, dated Dec 6 2011: quote exact, opening his paragraph on Kay's style; attribution, post number and date all match.

verdicts.trueWording: His best traits are his evocative prose, quality characterization and flair
verdicts.note: SFFWorld post #4 by TooNice, Dec 6 2011: quote exact (page continues 'for drama'); the same post carries the fast-paced/tight-narrative warning, though hedged there as 'probably won't be your cup of tea' where the claim states it flatly.

verdicts.trueWording: lovely, subtle differences in his tone and manner of writing
verdicts.note: SFFWorld post #2 by Severn, Dec 6 2011: quote exact; the same sentence names the back-to-back rereads (Tigana then The Last Light of the Sun), so the reread limb is supported.

verdicts.trueWording: he tries too hard to wow the reader with tons
verdicts.note: Goodreads message 8 by Josh, Feb 27 2009: quote exact; the same sentence carries 'come off as a little unnatural to me', 'tons of obscure words' and 'I'd rather just hear his honest voice as an author'.

verdicts.trueWording: his use of language is precise, and lyric, and highly creative
verdicts.note: Goodreads message 12 by Janny, Mar 12 2009: quote exact, preceded on the page by 'I have no issues at all with this author's style'. The page nowhere states Janny's gender, so the claim's 'she' is an outside inference, not a page fact.

verdicts.trueWording: a reader looking for a leaner prose style
verdicts.note: Goodreads message 12 by Janny: quote exact, in the Ysabel sentence; the page reads 'The pace is slightly quicker and less atmospheric', so 'quicker' is said of the pace and is hedged with 'slightly' the claim drops.

verdicts.trueWording: travels to a locale to soak up local color
verdicts.note: Goodreads message 12 by Janny (the claim's vaguer 'a member of the same topic' is accurate but under-specific): quote exact; the page continues 'then writes a fantasy based somewhat on the “theme” of the region', supporting the second limb. Page hedges with 'generally'.

verdicts.trueWording: very different from the often lean prose of The Fionavar Tapestry
verdicts.note: One Last Sketch, Tigana section: quote exact ('This is very different from...'), the referent being the Tigana prose just described; the post opens 'I found and finished every single novel by Guy Gavriel Kay', supporting the whole-run limb.

verdicts.trueWording: ornate style is cut down here to a much rougher use
verdicts.note: One Last Sketch, The Last Light of the Sun section: quote exact; the sentence continues 'of language rife with sentence fragments and strong images', supporting both the fragments and the strong-images limbs.

verdicts.trueWording: We’re all too often told how to feel
verdicts.note: One Last Sketch, Tigana section: quote exact; the same sentence continues with being hit by 'overwrought reminisces on the lost province of Tigana', supporting the second limb (claim says 'reminiscence').

verdicts.trueWording: long tangents describing the vast import of some historical moment
verdicts.note: One Last Sketch, Tigana section: quote exact; the page frames it as a 'tendency to go off on' such tangents 'which gets annoying', supporting the annoyance limb.

verdicts.trueWording: the prose often felt cold and clinical, even lacking in emotion
verdicts.note: Fantasy-Faction review by Alister Davison, 6 Jul 2013: quote exact; earlier in the same review 'Technically, it is superb, the prose flowing and lyrical' and later 'the technical aspects of the book and the author's skill with words are to be applauded', so both limbs of the split verdict hold.
